html:
SMTO-EXE-0148 — That app control doesn't support what SMTO tried to do

GUID: 4f1db6a9-20c5-59e1-975b-a9f2afca900f
Slug: ui-action-unsupported
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: ui

What happened

  • SMTO tried an action the button or field doesn't offer, like typing into something that isn't selected or clicking something that can't be pressed. SMTO didn't click or type anything.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If SMTO was trying to type, ask it to select (focus) the field first and then type. SMTO only types into a field that is already selected, so it never types into the wrong place.
  2. If it was trying to press or change something, tell SMTO another way the app offers to do it, for example a menu item instead of a button. Some apps don't let accessibility tools press every control, but often offer the same action elsewhere.
  3. If you only need one small step done, do it yourself in the app on that computer and tell SMTO when it's finished. This gets the task moving when the app doesn't allow that action at all.

What success looks like

  • SMTO's next step in the task completes the action, or the app shows the change you made yourself.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the app name and the action you wanted, to the person who manages that Gateway. Some apps simply don't allow this action through accessibility.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The native control lacks the requested semantic action/pattern or text interface, was not focused for exact-target keyboard input, or the platform rejected the selection/action variant.

What this means

  • The native control lacks the requested semantic action/pattern, text interface or required focus, or the platform rejected an unsupported selection/action variant. Only the existing explicit UI request may observe or mutate the selected desktop. Secure values stay redacted, stale references are not retargeted, and uncertain native input is not automatically repeated.

Why this can happen

  • The native control lacks the requested semantic action/pattern, text interface or required focus, or the platform rejected an unsupported selection/action variant.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect advertised element actions, platform pattern and focus rather than substituting a different action automatically.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the element's actions list and focused state in a fresh ui.element or ui.snapshot. Call ui.focus before key_press or type_text on an exact target, or choose a semantic action the element advertises (invoke, set_value, select, toggle, expand_collapse, scroll); deselecting a radio button is not supported.
  • Inspect the element actions and focus state. Use ui.focus before exact-target input, or choose a supported semantic action.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect the element actions and focus state. Use ui.focus before exact-target input, or choose a supported semantic action.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended supported action is available on the exact current target before dispatch.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, read secure fields, record input or bypass OS permissions.

Technical notes

  • Only the existing explicit UI request may observe or mutate the selected desktop. Secure values stay redacted, stale references are not retargeted, and uncertain native input is not automatically repeated.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
